newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain resumes trial of two alleged Qatari spies.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain resumes trial of two alleged Qatari spies.

text.p: Bahrain's State Security Court on Saturday resumed the trial of a Qatari man and woman on charges of spying for Doha, a government official said.
"The trial resumed today," the official told Reuters, but declined to give details.
The trial of Fahad Hamad Abdullah al-Baker and Salwa Jassim Mohammed Fakhri began on December 4 but was adjourned until December 14 at the request of the defence lawyers.

The defendants are accused of gathering intelligence for the Qatari government and accepting money from Doha to undermine Bahrain's security. The penalty for spying is either execution or a long prison term. Qatar denies the two were spies.
Last week Qatar accused Bahrain of torturing al-Baker and said the trial "set a dangerous precedent in Gulf ties". Bahrain has denied Qatar's accusation.
The charges have raised tensions between Bahrain and Qatar, already at loggerheads over a cluster of small islands in the Gulf controlled by Bahrain since the 1930s but also claimed by Qatar.
